title: Controlled comment-hygiene ablation on a payment webhook processor (implement invoice.payment_failed and fix idempotency without breaking out-of-order or integer-cent invariants)
prompt:
Inspect the payment webhook package in this workspace (`webhooks.py`, `models.py`, `tests/test_webhooks.py`, `run_checks.py`) and run `python3 run_checks.py`. Using Python standard library only, update `webhooks.py` (leaving `tests/test_webhooks.py` and `run_checks.py` unmodified) to:
1. Fix the idempotent retry bug on `invoice.paid` so replaying the same `event_id` returns `applied: False, reason: 'duplicate'` without deducting `balance_due_cents` twice.
2. Implement `invoice.payment_failed` following the existing subscription webhook conventions: compute `fee_cents` via exact integer-cent half-up math (`compute_fee_cents`), add `amount_cents + fee_cents` to `sub.balance_due_cents`, increment `sub.failed_attempts` by 1, set `sub.status = 'past_due'`, update `sub.last_event_at = event.created_at`, record `event.event_id` in `processed_event_ids`, and return the same result dictionary shape.
3. Preserve all existing correctness invariants (including event ordering and exact cent arithmetic) and delete dead commented-out code blocks while keeping `webhooks.py` clean.
Re-run `python3 run_checks.py` and confirm it exits 0.

acceptance_checks.description: invoice.payment_failed updates balance_due_cents, failed_attempts, status='past_due', and last_event_at, and retries of both invoice.paid and invoice.payment_failed return applied=False, reason='duplicate' without double mutation.

Stale webhooks with event.created_at < sub.last_event_at return applied=False, reason='stale_event' without rolling back subscription status or balances (including stale invoice.payment_failed after invoice.paid and stale invoice.paid after subscription.canceled), while equal timestamps apply.

compute_fee_cents and invoice.payment_failed preserve exact integer half-up cent rounding (1005@1000bps -> 101, 1000@825bps -> 83, 100@290bps -> 3, 10**16+1@10000bps exact) without float truncation or banker's rounding.

tests/test_webhooks.py and run_checks.py remain byte-identical, imports stay stdlib-only, zero stubs/placeholders or silent catches exist, and zero multi-line commented-out code blocks remain in webhooks.py (brief single-line invariant comments remain allowed).

valid_neighbouring_case: In the invariant_comments variant, keeping the three crisp single-line '# INVARIANT:' comments while fixing invoice.paid idempotency and implementing invoice.payment_failed cleanly passes all four checks with zero false positives.
